title: Global finite length for a fraction-field submodule
statement: Let R be a domain with fraction field K, and let M be an R-submodule of K^{\oplus r} for a nonnegative integer r. If R is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of Krull dimension 1 [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], then for every nonzero x in R the R-module M/xM has finite length [def-weil-pbc-module-length].

proof.text: Let S be the maximal ideals containing x. It is finite by [lem-sc-finite-maximals-over-element]; no separate unit reduction is necessary.
Set Q=M/xM. The scalar x annihilates Q. If a maximal ideal m does not contain x, x is a denominator for localization at m, so every q in Q becomes zero in Q_m. Thus Q_m is zero outside S.

For m in S, set A=R_m. Its height equals one: the nonzero x in m gives 0<m, while dim R=1 bounds the height above. Mathlib identifies dim A with this height. A is a Noetherian local domain. The localization lift A to K gives its fraction-field algebra structure. Localizing M inside K^r along the identity map produces an A-submodule L and its localization map f. The image of x remains nonzero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dim-one-submodule-quotient-finite-length] to L. Localization commutes with quotient, and the localized submodule xM is (image x)L by localized'_smul and localized'_span. The universal property gives an A-linear equivalence Q_m with L/(image x)L; transfer finite length along this equivalence.

Apply [lem-sc-finite-length-finite-maximal-support] to Q and S. It transfers both chain conditions along the localization order embedding into the finite product of the local submodule lattices, and concludes finite global length [def-weil-pbc-module-length].
